(b) `wireLiveXformField(id,apply)` (10669-10673): registers TWO listeners on the same element — `input` calls `apply(this,started)` then sets the closure-local `started=true`; `change` resets `started=false`. Because `input` fires on every drag-scrub tick AND `change` fires once at gesture end (mouseup/blur), a single scrub gesture calls `apply` many times with `started` false only on the FIRST call, true on every subsequent call within the same gesture — `started` IS the `skipUndo` flag: the five callers (`activeXformApplyMove/Scale/Rotate`, 10685-10720) forward it verbatim as each dispatch target's own `skipUndo` parameter, and every concrete applier (`selPropsApplyMove/Scale/Rotate`, timeline.js:3862/3885/3898; `nodeSelApplyMove/Scale/Rotate`, tools.js:1074/1086/1110) guards its own `pushUndo()` call with `if(!skipUndo)` — confirmed by direct read of all six applier bodies. Net effect: one scrub gesture = exactly one `pushUndo()` (on the first `input` tick) regardless of how many ticks follow, and the NEXT gesture on the same field gets its own fresh undo entry because `change` reset `started` to false in between. Vertex-mode dispatch table (10680-10684): `activeXformVertexMode()` returns true iff `state.tool==='subselect'&&_nodeSel.length>0` (tools.js:917's global, populated by subselect-bridge.js's own drag/click handlers, C04a); when true, `activeXformBounds`/`ApplyMove`/`ApplyScale`/`ApplyRotate` each call the tools.js `nodeSel*` sibling (`nodeSelBounds` tools.js:986, `nodeSelApplyMove` tools.js:1074, `nodeSelApplyScale` tools.js:1086, `nodeSelApplyRotate` tools.js:1110); when false (Select tool, or Subselect with nothing vertex-picked), each calls the timeline.js `selProps*` sibling instead (`selPropsApplyMove` timeline.js:3862, `selPropsApplyScale` timeline.js:3885, `selPropsApplyRotate` timeline.js:3898, `xformSelBounds` tools.js:1178) — see the reconciliation entry above for the select-bridge.js/subselect-bridge.js naming correction.

(c) Proportional size lock (`_spSizeLockOn`, 10693-10719): a plain closure-local boolean (not `state.*`, not persisted), toggled by `btn-sp-size-lock`'s own `.on` CSS class (10694-10697, same convention as the Document panel's `btn-dims-lock`). `sp-w`'s own handler (10698-10708) computes `sx=nv/b.width` from the live bound returned by `activeXformBounds()`; when the lock is on AND the bound's height is at least 0.01, it writes `sp-h`'s OWN field value to `Math.round(b.height*sx)` (a display-only echo, not itself an `input` dispatch) and calls `activeXformApplyScale(sx,sx,b.topLeft,started)` — both axes scaled by the SAME factor `sx`, i.e. the lock derives the ratio from the ACTIVE field's own delta every tick rather than from a remembered aspect ratio (contrast with the Document panel's `_dimsLockRatio`, C19ag:10495-10499, which snapshots `canvasW/canvasH` once at lock-on time). `sp-h`'s handler (10709-10719) is the exact mirror, computing `sy=nv/b.height` and locking width to `sy`. Anchor for the scale in BOTH cases is `b.topLeft` (the live bound's own top-left corner, fixed regardless of the anchor-grid's own pivot preset — the size fields always scale from the top-left, only ROTATION uses `xformAnchorPoint`). Anchor grid (`renderXformAnchorGrid`, 10725-10733): re-derives which of the 9 `.xa-dot` buttons gets the `.xa-active` class from `state.xformAnchorKey` (default `'mc'`→center, app.js:257), but ONLY when `!state.xformAnchorCustom` — a custom Alt+click anchor (select-bridge.js) suppresses the preset highlight entirely rather than misleadingly keeping a stale dot lit. A dot click (10734-10745) writes `state.xformAnchorKey=btn.dataset.key` (one of `tl/tc/tr/ml/mc/mr/bl/bc/br`, index.html:457-465), clears `state.xformAnchorCustom`, ALSO stamps `p.data.xformAnchorKey` on every currently `selectedPaths` entry (persisted per-stroke, same convention as the canvas Alt-drag path) and `saveActiveLayerFrame()`s if any path is selected, then re-renders the grid and the transform handles/engine frame. `xformAnchorPoint(b)` (tools.js:1383-1386, NOT in this scope, cited by name/line only) resolves the actual pivot Point: `state.xformAnchorCustom` if set, else `b[XFORM_ANCHOR_PROP[state.xformAnchorKey]||'center']` where `XFORM_ANCHOR_PROP` (tools.js:1376) maps each of the 9 keys to a Paper.js Rectangle property name (e.g. `tl`→`topLeft`, `mc`→`center`).

(d) `#align-toolbar .align-btn[data-align]` values (index.html:418-424): `left`/`centerH`/`right`/`top`/`centerV`/`bottom`, dispatched to `alignSelection(mode)` (tools.js:1297-1322, NOT in this scope, cited by name/line only) — requires 2+ selected paths, unites their bounds via `xformSelBounds()`, then translates each path (plus its fill gradient, vector-brush centerline, linked-fill companion, and brush texture dabs) so its own edge/center matches the union bound's corresponding edge/center on the requested axis; a no-op (nothing moved) pops the just-pushed undo entry back off. `#align-toolbar .align-btn[data-distribute]` values (index.html:431-432): `horizontal`/`vertical`, dispatched to `distributeSelection(mode)` (tools.js:1335+, NOT in this scope, cited by name/line only) — same per-path translate/companion-list convention as `alignSelection`, using EQUAL-GAP spacing with the first/last object (by current edge position) as fixed anchors, per its own lead-in comment (tools.js:1325-1334).

(e) `wireBoolBtn(id,mode)` (10762-10767): registers one `click` listener per button that branches on `e.altKey` — Alt/Option+click AND `window.SMGroup` truthy calls `SMGroup.combineSelection(mode)` (group-bridge.js:321, NOT in this scope, cited by name/line only), a non-destructive compound-shape-style grouping (mirrors Illustrator's Alt+Pathfinder convention per the lead-in comment, 10758-10761); a plain click (or Alt+click with `SMGroup` unavailable) calls `window.SM.booleanOp(mode)` (tools.js:5962, cited by name/line only), the pre-existing DESTRUCTIVE boolean, byte-for-byte unchanged by this feature. Four calls wire the four modes (10768-10771): `btn-bool-unite`→'unite', `btn-bool-subtract`→'subtract', `btn-bool-intersect`→'intersect', `btn-bool-exclude`→'exclude' — identical mode strings feed both the combine-group and the destructive-boolean branch.

(f) `applyVectorBrushToSelection(preset)` (10782-10805): eligibility (10792) is `p instanceof Path && !(p.data&&(p.data.isVectorBrush||p.data.isFillShape)) && (p.strokeColor||(p.data&&(p.data.brushTexturePreset||p.data.bitmapBrushSpec)))` — excludes vector-brush DAB copies and fill-only shapes outright (those are companion objects, not anchors), then requires either a real `strokeColor` OR an existing texture tag on the anchor itself (catching a fill-camouflaged, already-textured anchor whose `strokeColor` was nulled by the SAME camouflage convention, CLAUDE.md §1 — the lead-in comment, 10783-10791, documents this as a FIX: `strokeColor` alone used to gate eligibility and silently excluded exactly the strokes someone would want to re-convert). 'Strip' (`stripAnyBrushTexture`, app.js:1017-1023, NOT in this scope, cited by name/line only) removes any existing `brushCompanions` (each `.remove()`d then the array nulled), restores `opacity`/`strokeColor` from `preTextureOpacity`/`preTextureStroke` if the camouflage set them, and deletes `brushTexturePreset`/`bitmapBrushSpec`/`brushGroupId`/`bitmapPressureProfile` — applied to every eligible path FIRST (10801), THEN `applyBrushTexture(p,preset)` (tools.js:5149, NOT in this scope, cited by name/line only) re-applies if `preset` is truthy and not `'none'` (10802), so re-picking a different preset (or switching from a Bitmap Brush stroke, whose own tag `stripAnyBrushTexture` also strips identically) is a real conversion, never a silent no-op. Order: one `pushUndo()` (10794, BEFORE the per-path loop, so the whole selection's conversion is one undo step) → strip+reapply loop → `saveActiveLayerFrame();updateUI();showToast(SM.t('toastBrushAppliedToSel'))` (10804, all three same statement, in that order) → exposed as `window.SM.applyVectorBrushToSelection` (10806). Caller: a recursive `grep -rn "applyVectorBrushToSelection" src/js/` (all subdirectories) finds NO live call site anywhere — only this scope's own definition (10782) and export (10806), plus two comments in brush-menu-bridge.js (285, 305) that explicitly document NOT calling it ('NOT window.SM.applyVectorBrushToSelection(key) too — selectPreset ... already retroactively re-textures the current selection itself ... calling both double-applies'), and one descriptive (non-executed) sentence in index.html:1019 prose. The floating Brush panel (brush-menu-bridge.js:270-291/296-311) instead calls `window.BrushPresetPicker.selectPreset(key)` (brush-preset-picker.js:202-216), which calls `window.SM.setBrushPreset(key)` (timeline.js:683, NOT in this scope) — `setBrushPreset`'s OWN body (per brush-preset-picker.js's own comment, 205-215, dated 2026-07-17) already retroactively re-textures the current selection with its own `pushUndo`/strip/reapply, so calling `applyVectorBrushToSelection` too would double-apply. This CONTRADICTS the issue's own claim of 'its single caller (brush-menu-bridge.js)' — recorded here as an evidence-based correction: at the pinned frozen SHA, `applyVectorBrushToSelection` has ZERO live callers in src/js; it is reachable only via `window.SM.applyVectorBrushToSelection(...)` typed directly (e.g. a script/console call), not from any wired UI path found by this grep.

(g) Canvas/view toggles: `btn-clip`→`window.SM.setCanvasClip` (timeline.js:843, sets `state.canvasClip`) — NOT persisted to localStorage or exportJSON (app.js:127 default false only; timeline.js:2112's exportJSON `JSON.stringify` object literal does not reference `canvasClip`); read by `engine-bridge.js:2409` (`if (state.canvasClip) layers.push({items:buildClipMaskItems()})`), placed UNCONDITIONALLY (not gated by `includeEditorOverlays`) — confirmed by direct read that this line sits BEFORE the `if (includeEditorOverlays)` block (2412) — so the opaque overflow-hiding mask IS part of both live render and export/`render_to_pixels` output, despite its own lead-in comment (engine-bridge.js:2401-2407) calling it 'purely cosmetic'. `btn-safety`→`window.SM.setSafetyZones` (timeline.js:844, sets `state.safetyZones`) — also not persisted (same app.js:127 line, absent from exportJSON's stringify); read by `buildSafetyZoneItems()` (engine-bridge.js:2896-c.2920), called from inside the `if (includeEditorOverlays)` block (2482, confirmed by direct read of the enclosing scope) — its own comment (2894) states 'Pure overlay guide, never part of the actual rendered/exported frame', consistent with the gate. `btn-rulers`→`SMRulers.toggleOn()` (rulers-bridge.js:385-391) — sets `state.rulersOn`, PERSISTED to its own dedicated `localStorage['nemo-rulers-on']` key (rulers-bridge.js:375-377, a workspace preference explicitly documented as 'must NOT ride along in the project file', rulers-bridge.js:370-373) — read only by rulers-bridge.js's own DOM-canvas ruler/guide drawing (a separate `<canvas>` overlay outside the WebGPU scene entirely, not by engine-bridge.js/buildSceneJson); no `SMEngineBridge.renderNow()` call in `toggleOn` itself. `btn-alphabg`→inline toggle of `state.previewAlphaBg` (10842, this scope's own code, not a `window.SM.*` setter) — explicitly session-only, NOT persisted anywhere (app.js:148-154's own comment: 'Session-only by design ... same category as view.zoom/center'); read by `engine-bridge.js:796/811` (`buildSceneJson`'s own `alphaBg`/`showAlphaChecker` locals), and this handler calls `SMEngineBridge.renderNow()` itself (10844) rather than delegating to a `window.SM.*` setter.

(h) Duplicate `#p-cw`/`#p-ch` wiring: C19ag's own range wires BOTH ids' `input` event (C19ag 10508/10516) to apply the new canvas size LIVE during a scrub-drag, additionally updating the sibling field's value when `_dimsLockRatio` (the Document panel's OWN aspect-lock, unrelated to this scope's `_spSizeLockOn`) is set; this scope's own range (10818-10819) wires the SAME two ids' `change` event to `window.SM.setCanvasSize` again, WITHOUT any aspect-lock handling of its own. Because a browser fires `input` on every keystroke/drag tick and ALSO fires one final `change` on blur/Enter for the same `<input type=number>` element, both listeners DO fire for a single user gesture: `change`'s own `parseInt(this.value)` reads the value `input` already applied (and the OTHER axis's `state.canvasW`/`canvasH` that `input` already wrote, if the lock was engaged), so the second `setCanvasSize` call is redundant but not corrupting — it recomputes the identical `(w,h)` pair and re-runs `drawStage()`/`syncDocFields()` (setCanvasSize's own body, timeline.js:842) a second time for the same gesture.
